text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR first. It tests against the broadest historical data, catching edge cases that newer PRs might miss. The trade-off is slower feedback for the newest PRs, but we prioritize reliability over speed. This ensures we validate the system’s long-term performance before iterating.

name: Gauge
text: Running PR-Agent on the oldest merged PR tests a stale routing/prompt stack—risking false negatives from outdated logic, not edge cases. Better: run it on the newest *open* PR in shadow mode to catch *new* edge cases before they ship. Settle it by checking if the newest PR’s routing/prompts differ from the oldest’s; if they do, the newest PR is the higher-value test.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *both* the oldest merged PR *and* the newest open PR simultaneously—this splits the workload without sacrificing either historical edge-case coverage or new-edge detection. The trade-off is slightly higher compute cost, but it halves the time to validate the system’s full range of behavior.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest *open* PR first. It catches fresh edge cases before they ship, which is the highest-value failure to prevent. The trade-off is missing some historical edge cases, but those are less likely to break production now. This aligns with the goal of catching issues before they impact users.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first, then the oldest merged PR, to balance catching new edge cases and historical coverage. The result must deliver a validated system with minimal false negatives and a list of auto-applied safe changes, which the lead owns and will review for quality and task-relative value.
